editorial: Every time you think a historical epic ends with battlefield glory, Napoleon (2023) surprises you with a quiet, relentless obsession. The film renders the famed general as an addict to power, framing his rise and fall through his emotional addiction to Josephine. Joaquin Phoenix carries the film with almost no dialogue, letting his gestures and harsh stare haunt you. You, the history aficionado who craves deep psychological portraitures over endless tactics, will find yourself drawn into its raw intensity.
targetAudience: Ideal for history lovers craving psychological depth in iconic figures.
